q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026, after market close. Today is August 26, 2026. Resolution is essentially **immediate** — guidance will be issued today/tonight. This is asking for a live forecast of something about to happen in hours.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** issued during the Q2 FY2027 earnings release (which is happening today). Based on the research provided:

- NVIDIA issued Q2 FY2027 guidance on May 20, 2026 of **$91.0B ± 2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B)
- Wall Street consensus is **$91.9B** (roughly 60 analysts) and Zacks at **$91.8B**
- The research explicitly notes that "Q3 FY2027 outlook from management may be more impactful than the Q2 revenue figures themselves"

The question is asking for guidance on **Q3 FY2027** revenue (forward guidance issued during the Q2 earnings call).

NVIDIA has demonstrated consistent execution and typically provides guidance that is achievable but at the upper end of analyst expectations. Given:
- The strong demand environment for AI chips
- The pattern of meeting/beating guidance
- Wall Street consensus pointing to ~$91.8–91.9B for Q2 actual results
- Historical growth rates in this business

For **Q3 FY2027 forward guidance**, I would expect NVIDIA to guide in the range of **$95–102B**, reflecting:
- Sequential growth from Q2 (~5–10% typical)
- Strong data center demand
- Conservative guidance cushion (as is NVIDIA's pattern)

The center of the guidance range (99.5–115.5B) suggests forecasters expect guidance around **107.5B**, which reflects confidence in sustained strong demand and potential upside surprise.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: Significant slowdown in enterprise AI spending or data center capex
- **China exposure concerns**: Weakness in ability to serve China market or geopolitical constraints tightening further
- **Customer inventory corrections**: Evidence of oversupply or demand normalization
- **Competitive pressure**: Significant market share losses to AMD or other competitors
- **Conservative reset**: Management choosing to be more cautious after a strong run

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Accelerating demand**: Evidence of stronger-than-expected AI adoption across cloud and enterprise
- **Pricing power**: Ability to maintain or raise average selling prices
- **Supply visibility**: Removal of supply constraints enabling higher revenue
- **Market expansion**: New customer categories or use cases ramping faster than expected
- **M&A optionality**: Potential for consolidated/higher-margin product mix
- **Crypto/gaming uptick**: Unexpected strength in non-data-center segments

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides NVIDIA's most recent guidance:
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued May 20, 2026: **$91.0B ± 2%**
- Historical pattern: NVIDIA typically guides conservatively and beats

No specific historical pattern for Q3 guidance ranges is provided in the research. However, sequential Q-to-Q growth in NVIDIA's data center business has ranged 5–15% in recent cycles.

---

## Reasoning on the forecast range

The provided range of **99.5B to 115.5B** is quite wide (16B span), centering around 107.5B. This suggests significant uncertainty about the forward guidance.

Given that:
1. Q2 actual will likely be ~$91–92B (meeting upper end of prior guidance)
2. Sequential growth of 8–10% would suggest Q3 guidance of $98–101B
3. The upper end of the range (115.5B) would require 25%+ sequential growth (unlikely)
4. The range center (107.5B) implies ~17% sequential growth (possible but optimistic)

The most likely forward guidance will reflect:
- Continued strong but not explosive demand
- Conservative but achievable targets
- Probably in the **$99–105B range** for Q3

This maps to roughly the lower-to-middle portion of the provided range.

NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after the US market closes, with an analyst call following at 2 p.m. PT [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026), [ig.com](https://www.ig.com/en-ch/news-and-trade-ideas/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview--what-to-watch-260825).

NVIDIA's own guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% (a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion) [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026).

Wall Street consensus estimates for Q2 FY2027 revenue are slightly higher, with an average of $91.9 billion across roughly 60 analysts [ig.com](https://www.ig.com/en-ch/news-and-trade-ideas/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview--what-to-watch-260825), and Zacks consensus at $91.8 billion [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). This implies that meeting analyst expectations requires NVIDIA to land in the upper half of its own guided range [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). Analysts indicate that the Q3 FY2027 outlook from management may be more impactful than the Q2 revenue figures themselves [ig.com](https://www.ig.com/en-ch/news-and-trade-ideas/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview--what-to-watch-260825).
